skillSays: Before animating, answer an 8-step checklist: emotional target, one motion-personality archetype, primary property, duration, easing family, hero element, secondary and ambient layers, and the 1/3 rules.
Pick ONE archetype and keep it consistent (Corporate is the UI default: 200-400ms, cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), 0-3% overshoot).
Build every animation in three layers: primary action, secondary support (shadow, icon, trailing text), and ambient life.
Entrances decelerate and exits accelerate; exits are 65-75% of the entrance; never linear for spatial motion, never opacity-only for important changes.
Stagger budgets: micro cascade 20-40ms with a total under 200ms; never exceed 500ms; at most one third of elements move at once and nothing travels over a third of the screen.
Provide a reduced-motion alternative and a duration palette of three values.

changes: Archetype chosen: Corporate. Signature curve cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), exit curve cubic-bezier(0.3,0,1,1), duration palette 140 / 250 / 400ms.
Primary: toast slides 28px from the right + opacity in 250ms; exit is 180ms ease-in (72% of the entrance, inside the 65-75% rule).
Secondary layer: shadow arrives 50ms later, icon scales 0.6 to 1 in 100ms after a 50ms delay, the tick draws over 160ms at +130ms, text trails by 80ms.
Ambient layer: a linear 3.6s countdown bar (linear allowed for progress), the other rows dim to 85% and the booked row washes teal over 250ms (staging).
Primary container: scale(0.94) + translateY(-4px) to rest from the top-right corner in 200ms; exit 140ms ease-in (70%).
Secondary: items cascade 30ms apart starting 50ms after the container (90ms stagger span, inside the micro-cascade budget), each 160ms with a 4px rise; the trigger dots rotate 90 degrees in 200ms.
Ambient: the list behind recedes to 80% opacity while open (200ms in, 140ms out); item hover is 80ms (hover under 100ms).
Reduced motion becomes a 120ms opacity-only variant.
Card entrance recipe per the skill: 20px below + opacity in 250ms on the signature curve, shadow lands 50ms later, row content fades in 100ms later.

Success state on check-off: checkbox pops 1.12 and back (220ms), fills in 140ms, tick draws 180ms at +60ms, strike follows 200ms at +80ms; ambient layer is a progress bar that eases to done/total over 300ms.
Removal: collapse exit (scale 0.95 + opacity) 180ms ease-in, then the rest shift up in a 30ms-stepped cascade of 200ms ease-in-out starting at +80ms (exit/entrance overlap).
Empty state fades in over 250ms and out over 140ms; every duration comes from the 140/250/400 palette or the skill's tables.

skillSays: It is a pipeline for turning AI-generated video or frame sequences into web animation driven by scroll, pointer, drag, audio, data or time.
Start by locking a concept contract: driver, time_control (scrub, segment-play or autonomous), input semantics, rest state and reduced-motion state.
Keep timing in one manifest (states, segments, hold times). Pages and controllers read it and never keep a second set of constants.
Pick the delivery format (alpha atlas, chroma video, baked video) and the runtime controller separately, via a budget script.
Pilot first on the real page, then QA reverse playback, cold cache, DPR, mobile and failure cases.
It explicitly declines pure CSS/JS interface transitions and micro-interactions and hands those to ordinary front-end code.

changes: The skill's own scope rule marks a toast as plain UI motion, so no AI media was generated (the pipeline also needs a ZenMux key); only its contract and manifest ideas were applied
All timing sits in one TL manifest of segments (start, end, curve) and render(t) is a pure function of time, so the page keeps no second timeline
An autonomous controller advances t on requestAnimationFrame and loops; reduced motion renders the manifest's rest state once and hides Replay
Same out-of-scope outcome as motion-1: built as ordinary front-end code, with the skill's controller and manifest structure as the only borrowed parts
Cursor travel, menu open, item stagger, highlight steps and close are separate manifest segments with named curves, rendered together from one t
Because render(t) is deterministic the sequence can be seeked and replayed from any frame without state to reset
Out of scope for the skill (UI micro-interaction): no generated media, manifest-driven vanilla JS instead
Typing, add, two check-offs and two removals are segments; row positions are derived from removal progress, so rows below slide up by transform only
Rest state is defined up front (a stable mid-sequence frame) and used as the reduced-motion view

skillSays: Write focused, reusable Playwright scripts and run them through the skill's run.js executor (or inline with -e), instead of ad-hoc one-liners
Detect running dev servers first with helpers.detectDevServers(); use the only result automatically, ask when there are several or none
Prefer user-facing locators in order: getByRole with a name, getByLabel, getByText, getByTestId; rely on auto-waiting, not sleeps or networkidle
Report actions, failures and artifact paths, and never claim success without checking the resulting page
Visible browser by default, headless only when asked or when there is no display; PW_* env vars control headless, channel, artifact and script dirs
Run `npm run setup` once to install Playwright and Chromium

changes: Wrote one script with getByLabel/getByRole locators that reads the resulting DOM after each submit, so the report states what the page actually showed for the invalid and valid cases
Listened to page requests during the flow and found the 'account created' success never hits a server
Used the inline -e mode for a quick probe and confirmed the email is injected with innerHTML (an payload really executed)
Flagged that detectDevServers() returned the macOS AirPlay listener on :5000 instead of the app, and used the known URL
Attached console, pageerror, request and response listeners before the first click, so the TypeError was captured at the moment it happened
Compared clicking Book with and without selecting a slot first, which isolates the cause (selected is undefined until a slot click)
Confirmed the server side saw exactly one POST, only in the second scenario
Noticed the success banner appears even when the response is a 501 (res.ok is never checked)

skillSays: Rules are ranked by impact: eliminate request waterfalls and bundle size first (CRITICAL), re-renders and JS micro-optimisations last
Run independent async work with Promise.all instead of awaiting one request after another
Avoid heavy or barrel imports (lodash, whole chart libraries) and load heavy components lazily, only when the feature is used
Keep frequently changing state (a ticking clock) out of the big component, memoise rows, use stable callbacks via functional setState and a deferred value for search input
Replace repeated find() calls and chained filter/sort passes with Map lookups and a single loop; keep effect dependencies narrow
Each rule is a short incorrect/correct code pair with an impact label, so changes can be tied to a named rule

changes: Fixed the three sequential fetches with Promise.all (+ AbortController): last response on screen at 247 ms instead of 1624 ms in the mocked benchmark

Pulled the 1-second clock into its own component, memoised Row with a stable onCancel(id) and a deferred search value; React render time over 4 s of ticks dropped from about 1477 ms to 2 ms (4x CPU throttle, 1500 rows)
Dropped lodash and moment for Map and Intl, imported only the line-chart parts of Chart.js and lazy-loaded the chart: initial JS 168.6 KB gzip to 47.2 KB
While applying the effect-dependency rule I found the chart effect crashed the whole dashboard on the first tick (Canvas is already in use); fixed with [data] deps and chart.destroy()

The guide covers scripts, resource hints and idle work only, so the run said so: it removed the blocking jQuery and the unused moment, added preconnect for fonts and deleted the 3e7-iteration busy loop, then measured instead of assuming a win

Measurement showed those rules alone left first paint at about 3.4 s (the Google Fonts stylesheet still blocked it); a non-blocking stylesheet, which is outside the guide, brought FCP to 0.62 s and performance to 100
Rendered the testimonials in the HTML instead of injecting them after 1.5 s, trimmed the fonts to one family and two weights
Accessibility and SEO changes (lang, title, description, a real link and button, contrast) were made from general practice and flagged as not coming from the guide

skillSays: Animate between UI states with the browser's native document.startViewTransition; declare what animates with view-transition names/classes and style it in CSS.
Every transition must say what it communicates: shared element, reveal, list identity, enter/exit, or route change; if it says nothing, do not add it.
Use the provided timing vars (exit 150ms, enter 210ms, move 400ms) and ready-made recipes: fade, slide-up/down, scale-in/out, morph.
Give each list item its own unique name so siblings glide into their new spot; wrap displaced content so it glides instead of jumping.
Make the root a live capture (hide old root, no root animation) and set ::view-transition { pointer-events: none } so the page stays interactive and hover keeps working.
Always include the reduced-motion block; unsupported browsers just skip the animation.

changes: Toast and the booked slot change in ONE startViewTransition call: toast has view-transition-name: toast, class slide-up/slide-down; the slot is a named update so it cross-fades.

Enter uses the slide-up recipe: opacity 210ms ease-in plus translateY(32px) 400ms ease-in; exit uses slide-down: 150ms ease-out (fade + 16px). Dropped the recipe's 150ms enter delay because nothing is exiting beside it.
Root is live (::view-transition-old(root) hidden, new(root) animation none) and ::view-transition has pointer-events: none.
Reduced-motion block from the skill zeroes all view-transition durations.
Menu is a named view transition (menu) toggled with hidden inside startViewTransition; it uses the skill's scale recipes: scale-in 210ms ease-out from scale(0.85), scale-out 150ms ease-in.
transform-origin: top right set on both pseudo-elements so it grows from the trigger; enter delay removed (no paired exit).
The hover highlight inside the menu is deliberately not a view transition: unnamed content stays live under the transition.
view-transition-class holds both scale-in and scale-out so one element covers entering and leaving.
List identity pattern: every task li gets a unique view-transition-name (task-1, task-2, ...) so siblings glide up on removal with the 400ms ease-in-out group animation (--duration-move).
New rows use class fade-in (210ms ease-out), removed rows use fade-out (150ms ease-in), set per transition, because a class on an element that exists in both states would flash.
Layout displacement morph: the footer and the count pill are named too, so they glide or cross-fade instead of jumping; the empty-state is a named enter/exit.
Check-off is an update on the named row, so it cross-fades at 210ms; the root stays live so the typed input keeps updating.

skillSays: Design from fixed scales and never invent a value: a 4-8-12-16-24-32-48-64-96 spacing scale, a 12-72px type scale in px/rem, two font weights, five shadow elevations.
Build hierarchy with weight and colour instead of size: three text greys at most, one solid primary action, secondary as outline, tertiary as a link.
Use 8-10 grey shades and 5-10 shades per colour written in HSL, defined up front and never generated at runtime; flip contrast (dark text on a tint) instead of grey-on-colour.
Always put more space around a group than within it, shrink large elements faster than small ones on mobile, and give every functional border 3:1 contrast.
Never rely on colour alone: pair status colours with an icon or text, and put large icons inside coloured circles instead of scaling them up.

changes: Started from the skill's tokens.css and retuned the grey and primary ramps to a teal hue instead of picking colours ad hoc
Three-level button hierarchy in the hero: solid primary, outline secondary, underlined tertiary link
Feature icons sit in 48px tinted circles, and status chips pair colour with a check or clock icon
Real depth from a layered two-part shadow on the appointment card, with weight and grey shades doing the hierarchy rather than larger type
Clinic is emphasised by de-emphasising the others: outline buttons on Solo and Group, a solid primary and a stronger elevation on Clinic
Prices are large and bold while '/month' and 'Billed monthly' drop to tertiary grey, following 'emphasise by de-emphasising'
The toggle is a real switch with label text that changes weight, and the savings chip pairs green with text
Inputs are 44px with a 3:1 functional border (--border-strong) and a visible focus ring, separate from the decorative divider token
Errors use a red tint with dark red text and a circled icon, so colour is never the only signal, and help text is hidden while an error is shown
Spacing follows the scale throughout, with more space between fields than between a label and its input

skillSays: It is a router: video creation loads remotion-create, markup rules load remotion-markup, rendering loads remotion-render.

skillSays: Go mobile-first: base styles are the phone layout, min-width media queries enhance upward.
Use container queries (container-type: inline-size) so components respond to their own width, not the viewport.
Make type and spacing fluid with clamp() scales instead of fixed px at each breakpoint.
Reach for intrinsic CSS Grid (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(X,100%),1fr))) before adding breakpoints.
Use dvh/svh instead of 100vh, logical properties (inline/block), and 44px minimum touch targets.
Check for the usual failures: horizontal overflow, fixed px widths, tiny text, squished aspect ratios.

skillSays: This is a review-only skill: it measures motion code against ten non-negotiable standards (justified, frequency-appropriate, responsive easing, under 300ms, correct origin, interruptible, GPU-only, accessible, asymmetric, cohesive) and defaults to flagging; approval is earned.

Certain things are flagged on sight: transition: all, scale(0), ease-in on UI, keyframes on rapidly triggered UI, animated layout properties, ungated hover motion, missing prefers-reduced-motion, symmetric timing on press/release.

Fixes follow a strict preference order: delete the animation, reduce it, fix easing, fix origin/physicality, make it interruptible, move it to the GPU, make timing asymmetric, then polish and accessibility.
The review is a single Before / After / Why table, then a verdict grouped by impact tier ending in Block or Approve, with file:line citations and exact values from the standards.
Workflow used here: build a first draft, review it with the skill, then ship the fixed version.

changes: Review blocked the draft (@keyframes slideIn .5s ease-in-out, slideOut .4s ease-in, transition: all .4s); the shipped toast is a transition with @starting-style: enter 260ms, exit 160ms, both cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1).

Kept the toast sliding in from the right edge and leaving to the right (translateX(calc(100% + 24px))) so in and out share one axis; the draft's hover scale(1.05) on Book became scale(0.97) on :active with colour-only hover behind (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine).
Slot label crossfade went from transition: all .5s to opacity + blur(2px) over 200ms.
Added a prefers-reduced-motion branch that drops the translate and keeps a 150ms fade.

Draft opened from scale(0) with transform-origin: center and ease-in at 300ms (three escalation triggers at once). Shipped: scale(0.95) + opacity from the trigger's centre, 160ms open and 110ms close on cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1).
Followed the remedial order: deleted the translateX(4px) item hover entirely (step 1) instead of tuning it, leaving a 100ms background-colour change.
Keyboard open and Escape are instant (data-instant, 0ms); pointer open keeps the animation.
No stagger was added: the review only asks for one where everything arrives at once and this menu is opened too often to decorate.
Draft added each task with a 500ms keyframe pop from scale(0) overshooting to 1.08; shipped is a 180ms opacity + translateY(6px) transition.
Draft removed rows by animating height, margin and padding to 0 over 400ms ease-in; shipped fades out in 140ms then closes the gap with a transform-only FLIP, 200ms on cubic-bezier(0.77,0,0.175,1).
The tick and fill changed from transition: all .3s to 150ms background-color and opacity plus scale(0.8 to 1); the strikethrough is instant and the text colour fades (150ms).
Add button gets scale(0.97) on press; the ungated scale(1.05) hover was removed.

skillSays: Interview for subject, brand kit, art direction (default: soft clay isometric diorama), camera style, an ordered list of scenes and a budget.
Generate one still per scene, then dive clips and connector clips with an image-to-video model so the camera flies through one continuous world with no cuts.
Seams must be frame-identical: each clip starts on the actual last frame of the previous one.
A scrub engine maps scroll to video time with smoothing, pins eyebrow, headline, body and tags per scene, and adds a route rail.
Pacing knobs (scroll length, linger) let the camera settle while the copy peaks; reduced motion falls back to stills.
Always asks about a native 9:16 mobile chain and estimates cost before spending anything.

Theme by editing OKLCH CSS variables (--primary, --radius, --border, --ring) and the .dark class, never per-component dark: overrides.

skillSays: Slack message GIFs are not 128x128 emoji: pick dimensions deliberately (emoji 128x128, message ~480) and 10-30 fps, 48-128 colours
Build frames as PIL images and assemble them with GIFBuilder, which quantizes to one global palette and can drop near-duplicate frames

Use easing helpers for motion and thick lines / layered shapes so the graphics look polished, not placeholder

skillSays: Start from the reader's decision, then write an insight-led headline that is one proposition, not several claims joined by "and".
Name the comparison type (time series, ranking, correlation...) before choosing a pattern; the chart follows the question.
Fixed visual system on a 1280x720 canvas: white slide, one navy accent, grey for context, red only for risk, Georgia headline and Helvetica body, 22px reading-size floor.
Every mark carries information: honest zero baseline, direct labels instead of legends, no decorative bars, meaning never by colour alone.
Write an explicit implication line and a source line with assumptions; do not invent data, targets or sources.
Deliver the contract: strategic question, headline, recommended visualization, spec, data and assumptions, quality score.

skillSays: Configure the design system CSS-first: tokens in @theme (here mapped through the play-CDN config), not a hand-edited palette per component.
Use semantic OKLCH colour tokens (background, foreground, primary, muted, accent, destructive, border, ring, card) and write bg-primary or text-muted-foreground instead of raw colour utilities.
Organise components as base, then variants, then sizes, then states, with a shared radius scale and animation tokens (fade-in, slide-in).
Dark mode is a class that only overrides the token values; components never carry dark: colour overrides.
Build for accessibility and responsiveness: visible focus rings with offset, aria state, reduced-motion fallbacks, mobile-first grids.

Labels, aria-describedby, role=alert errors and a custom checkbox built on a peer sr-only input, so it stays keyboard accessible.

skillSays: Route the request through a table: always read player-contract.md, then the matching recipe (loaders/icons, logo, typography, data...) plus motion-taste and design-taste

Loaders are transparent by default, loop seamlessly over 60-120 frames, use phase offsets instead of lockstep motion, and keep geometry crisp at small sizes
Expose important values as slots (e.g. accentColor) with a controls.json label, and use real top-level keys (v, fr, ip, op, w, h, nm, assets, layers; op exclusive)
Derive easing from behaviour-based anchors rather than one uniform ease; verify frame 0, midpoint and op-1, and review the loop seam
Premium means subtract: zero chrome/container budget, one surface tone, one divider treatment

skillSays: Pick one of ten ready-made font and colour themes (Ocean Depths, Sunset Boulevard, Modern Minimalist and so on) instead of inventing a palette.

Use the theme file as the spec: a fixed set of four colours with roles (background, accent, secondary accent, text) and one header and body font.

If no preset fits, write a new named theme in the same format, show it for review, then apply it.

skillSays: Load three.js as ES modules through an import map; no script-tag builds.
Set up the renderer deliberately: capped pixel ratio, tone mapping, PCFShadowMap (the soft variant is deprecated), resize with updateProjectionMatrix.
Drive the loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop and a Timer (Clock is deprecated), and ease with frame-rate independent MathUtils.damp.
Use InstancedMesh for repeated objects and merge static geometry; keep draw calls low.
Procedural motion for simple scenes; AnimationMixer clips only for authored animation.
Dispose geometry, materials and textures, and release the renderer, when the scene goes away.

All easing (slots filling, pointer parallax) uses MathUtils.damp on a Timer delta, so it feels the same at 30 and 120 fps; the Timer also pauses while the tab is hidden

Physical materials get an image-based light built once from a tiny PMREM studio scene, then disposed; pagehide frees geometry, materials, environment and renderer; reduced motion draws one settled frame
Particles are a single Points object whose dynamic position buffer is updated per frame; settle progress is damped toward a target that time and scroll both push
Pixel ratio is capped at 2, fog fades the distant cloud, and the sprite texture is a CanvasTexture created once and disposed on pagehide

skillSays: Before writing any UI, look up each needed component (hero, form, card, select, toggle, badge...) in a 60+ component reference and follow its best practices.
Aim for modern, minimal, production-ready: restraint over decoration, an 8px spacing grid, one confident accent on a neutral palette.
Pair a distinctive display font with a clean body font and push weight contrast; avoid Inter/Roboto defaults, purple gradients and evenly spaced card grids.
Pick a design direction preset (Modern SaaS by default) and build real states: hover, focus, disabled, error, loading, empty.
Follow interaction rules: verb-first buttons, one primary per section, validate on blur, labels above inputs, 44px touch targets, WCAG AA contrast.
Avoid listed anti-patterns such as placeholder-only fields, equal-weight buttons, rainbow badges and disabled submit with no explanation.

Committed to Bricolage Grotesque 800 with tight tracking against Instrument Sans, and one cobalt accent on warm off-white.

skillSays: Start a new page by generating a design system from a search over its local database: run search.py --design-system with product type and keywords, which returns a landing pattern, a visual style, a palette with semantic tokens, a font pairing, key effects and anti-patterns.

Rank concerns by priority: accessibility and touch targets first (4.5:1 contrast, visible focus, labels, 44px targets), then performance, style consistency, layout, type and colour, motion, forms, navigation.
Use semantic colour tokens rather than raw hex, SVG icons not emoji, a 4/8px spacing scale, 150-300ms transitions, and respect prefers-reduced-motion.
For forms: visible labels, validate on blur, specific cause-plus-fix errors tied by aria-describedby, an error summary with focus management, and a show/hide password toggle.
Finish by running a pre-delivery checklist (cursor-pointer, hover states, contrast, focus, reduced motion, 375/768/1024/1440 layouts).

skillSays: Start from context: which screen, what the user is trying to do, how they feel, what tone and character limits apply.

skillSays: Fetch Vercel's current Web Interface Guidelines and check the UI file against every rule, reporting terse file:line findings

Focus: never remove outlines without a :focus-visible replacement; compound controls use :focus-within

Typography and motion: curly quotes, real ellipsis, non-breaking spaces, tabular-nums, balanced headings, no transition: all, honour prefers-reduced-motion
Content and state: Title Case headings and buttons, specific button labels, Intl number formatting, URL reflects state

skillSays: Review and write prose against Vercel's Writing Guidelines, fetched fresh from the source before each use.
Voice: active voice, "you" not "the user", imperative steps, contractions, sentences under about 20 words, no rhetorical questions.
Ban easy, simple, quick, very, just, really. Replace weasel words and vague quantifiers with a real number.
No em dashes or dashes as punctuation, curly quotes, a real ellipsis, spaced units (5 MB), sentence-case headings.
Flag AI tells: recap transitions, choppy stop-start fragments, spec-sheet voice, personified artifacts, template framing.
Open with a summary, keep paragraphs to 2 to 4 sentences, bold only for UI elements or a critical fact.
